bullets.title: Fed set to hike 25bp Wednesday; markets ~90% priced, SEP expected to show 2 hikes for 2026
bullets.body: Broad sell-side consensus (GS, MS, JPM, UBS, Piper Sandler) expects a 25bp September FOMC hike following a hawkish August CPI (core +0.29-0.30% MoM) and firmer PPI. Fed dot plot likely shows 2 hikes for 2026 median with December as the follow-on; hawks gaining influence and right-tail risk to rates elevated. JPM and MS note equities have largely repriced Fed expectations throughout the year, with 10Y at cycle highs near 4.99-5.0%.

bullets.title: Oil surges 3%+ to $102-103 WTI/$108 Brent on Saudi East-West pipeline Houthi attack; up to 4-5% global supply at risk
bullets.body: Houthi forces struck Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, halting exports with repair timeline estimated at 5-6 weeks; Houthis also captured Perim/Hanish islands in Bab el-Mandib. Diesel prices hit all-time high of $6.23/gal nationally. WTI up ~9.4% last week and +20.7% in 3 months; CRB commodities +14.4% in 3 months, creating stagflationary pressure on equities and bond yields.

bullets.title: AI safety 'pacing' call from Amodei/Altman/Musk sparks semi selloff; semis -4.7% pre-market, software rallies defensively
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend blog calling to 'pace the frontier' — explicitly not halt training — triggered a sharp rotation: NVDA -3%, MU/SNDK/INTC/AMD -5%, CRWV/NBIS -7% pre-market; software rallied (NOW +4.9%, CRM +3.2-3.4%, ADBE +2.4%). Consensus view across Jefferies, GS, JPM is that the knee-jerk is tactical weakness not a fundamental spending slowdown, with AI buildout remaining early-innings. Trump publicly rejected the AI guardrails push, emphasizing U.S.-China competitive dynamics.

bullets.title: NVDA in talks as ~$10B anchor investor in Anthropic IPO at ~$2T valuation; OpenAI delays IPO to 2027
bullets.body: Anthropic is targeting a Nasdaq listing raising up to $100B at ~$2T valuation, with Nvidia reportedly in talks to anchor with up to $10B. Anthropic posted positive adjusted operating income for the second consecutive quarter with gross margins exceeding 80%. OpenAI CEO Altman separately confirmed the company will not IPO in 2026 due to AI safety concerns.

bullets.title: Equity market regime: S&P near record highs at 19x P/E despite 10Y at 5%; bull market seen intact but tactically cautious into Fed
bullets.body: GS notes S&P 500 forward P/E compressed from 22x to 19x as 10Y approached 5%, but equity risk premiums are stable and stocks historically average +9% in the 12 months following a first Fed hike. JPM is tactically neutral into Wednesday with 10Y at cycle highs, noting it historically takes ~8 weeks for equities to digest yield moves. Breadth is oversold (only 22.6% of S&P above 20-day MA) within an intact uptrend per Oppenheimer technicals.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers outperforming AI infrastructure suppliers as market focuses on revenue/earnings timing over demand existence
bullets.body: Opco and JPM both flag a divergence: companies writing capex checks (MSFT targeting 38GW by 2032, AMZN doubling 2025 capacity by 2027, GOOGL ~$170B incremental TPU spend through 2028) are outperforming infrastructure beneficiaries. TSMC reported +53% YoY August sales. Market is focused on when revenues flow through to semis/networking vendors, not whether demand exists.

bullets.title: AI capex political/regulatory risk growing: ~500 jurisdictions with bans, $156B in projects delayed, Massachusetts 20MW+ moratorium
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags that AI infrastructure risk is shifting from capital/chips/power toward 'social and political permission to build.' ~500 jurisdictions have enacted bans or moratoriums on data centers; ~$156B in AI infrastructure projects were cancelled/delayed in 2025 and ~$130B affected in 1Q26. Massachusetts is implementing a moratorium on permitting data centers 20MW+ through November 2027. AI-related capex contributed ~0.6-0.8pp to GDP growth, representing ~one-third of overall growth.

bullets.title: 'Pause is the signal': AI capability acceleration (Jevons paradox) means Wall Street likely underestimates semiconductor demand
bullets.body: One note argues Astra's training on 100k+ Nvidia Grace Blackwell systems and Jensen Huang's AGI declaration signal accelerating underlying capability, not disappointment — and that a deliberate pause would paradoxically confirm that. Improved AI efficiency historically increases total compute consumption (Jevons paradox). Wall Street models likely underestimate semiconductor demand; WFE spending could reach multiples of pre-AI baseline. Physical bottlenecks (electricity, cooling, copper, land) now constraining, not GPU availability.

bullets.title: Memory structural undersupply worsening: DRAM S/D deficit -8.7%/-9.7% in 2027E/2028E; HBM demand +62-69% YoY
bullets.body: Citi forecasts AI continual learning drives persistent HBM, server DDR5, and eSSD undersupply through 2031. Global DRAM demand grows +30%/+35% YoY in 2027E/2028E vs. supply of only +19%/+22%; NAND S/D also negative at -6.1%/-5.5%. Top beneficiaries: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Sandisk; SPE/materials: AMAT, Lam Research.

bullets.title: Hawkish CPI/PPI + oil above $100 driving multi-DM hiking cycle; JPM Taylor rule suggests rates 100bp too low
bullets.body: JPMorgan Global Data Watch finds eight of nine DM central banks projected to hike by year-end; Taylor rule analysis suggests DM policy rates ~100bp below macroeconomic fundamentals. Core goods inflation forecast to rise from 1.5% annualized in 1H26 to 2.5% in 2H26; oil sustained at $100/bbl imparts a stagflationary impulse. UST 2Y +26bp to cycle highs; 10Y +19bp to cycle highs last week; yield curve at cycle lows (flattened 7bp).

bullets.title: 10Y yields can rise to ~5-6% before equity de-rating given 28% 2026 EPS growth; but 4-5 hike cycle would create material downside
bullets.body: JPM strategy notes S&P 500 is up 16% this year on 28% 2026 EPS growth and 21% 2027 EPS growth, even as 30Y yields hit ~5.40% (highest in ~20 years). A shallow 1-2 hike cycle is manageable; a 4-5 hike scenario creates material equity downside. Corporate interest expense impact is gradual given fixed/long-dated debt, offset by Financials profitability and ~$2.4T in cash balances.

bullets.title: Stocks-bonds correlation deeply negative at above-trend GDP; non-AI cyclicals underperforming, AI buildout basket outperforming
bullets.body: 22V Research notes real GDP at 4.6% (Atlanta Fed) is well above the ~2% 'speed limit,' so strong growth shows up in higher yields and restrictive Fed policy rather than equity prices — creating deeply negative stock-bond correlation. Non-AI cyclicals (Retail, Transports, Housing) underperform; AI Buildout (Semis, Power, Cooling) and AI Services baskets are the right positioning. 2027 total AI capex projected at $1.26T (+44.8% YoY).

bullets.title: Hedgeye turns bearish: QQQ/SPY signaling bearish trades, NVDA flips Neutral, AMZN/GOOGL/TSLA/NFLX downgraded to bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye Risk Range Signals show QQQ breaking TREND support (level 705), SPY signaling bearish trade (author sold all longs except one), and NVDA flipping from Bullish to Neutral. AMZN, GOOGL, NFLX, TSLA all downgraded to bearish trend; MSFT, AAPL, META remain bullish. IWM already broke TREND support. KOSPI down 27% from June AI bubble peak.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: Post-CPI equity rotation is mid-cycle quality broadening, not return of early-cycle semi leadership
bullets.body: MS macro forum concludes the back-up in rates was driven by rate repricing and a hot economy; US equities have already repriced Fed expectations throughout the year. The broadening equity trade is a mid-cycle quality rotation, not a return to early-cycle semiconductor leadership. Rate differentials (not terms of trade) driving EUR/USD; FOMC is the key swing factor for the dollar.

bullets.title: Housing market deteriorating: homebuilder ETF -21.7% YoY, mortgage rates 6.76-6.85%, purchase apps -4.2% YoY
bullets.body: JPM housing tracker shows 30Y mortgage rates at 6.76-6.85% (+41bp YoY, 85th percentile), third straight weekly increase. Purchase applications -4.2% YoY on 4-week MA; refinance apps -32.1%. New listings collapsed 5.5pp YoY; cancellations at 14.8% (93rd percentile). Homebuilder index -4% on the week, -21.7% YoY, underperforming S&P by 32.6pp over LTM.

bullets.title: AI lab CEO 'frontier pacing' debate becoming U.S. midterm political issue; legislative proposals to ban/pause ASI introduced
bullets.body: Anthropic's Amodei, OpenAI's Altman, and Musk publicly backing AI development pacing; legislative proposals introduced by Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar to ban artificial superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development. Jefferies and others flag AI safety/data center pushback as an increasingly core theme in U.S. midterms. Trump is resisting guardrails, framing it as a U.S.-China competitiveness issue. Silicon Valley leadership is split on motives.

bullets.title: US LNG: Exxon targets 30% global market share by 2030; Brent LNG prices unlikely to fall in next 6 months
bullets.body: Exxon SVP stated U.S. LNG supply will reach 30% of global market by 2030; Chevron Australia President sees LNG prices unlikely to decline over next 6 months as energy-security-concerned buyers lock in supply. Venture Global signed a new 20-year 0.5 Mtpa deal with China Gas, bringing total offtake to 2.5 Mtpa. Natural gas TTF +5.0% to 83.24 euros/MWh on weather/supply concerns.

bullets.title: AI power semis TAM rising to $13-15B by 2028-2030; UBS prefers TXN and ADI over Infineon; grid capacity the real bottleneck
bullets.body: UBS raises AI data-center power semis TAM to $13B by 2028E (vs. $11B prior) and $15B by 2030E, with content per GW rising from $95M to $150-170M/GW. Grid capacity may be the actual bottleneck — model implies 51GW added in 2027 and 105GW in 2030 vs. market expectations of 30-50GW annually. TXN (PSU/IBC share gains) and ADI (VRM expansion) preferred; Infineon rated Neutral on high expectations.

bullets.title: GS Communacopia: AI demand broadening from hyperscalers to neoclouds, enterprises, sovereigns; enterprise shifting from experimentation to production
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes AI demand is broadening rather than slowing across hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises, and sovereign customers. Agentic AI is materially increasing bandwidth requirements for networking vendors. Enterprise AI deployments are moving from experimentation toward production, and AI adoption in internet companies is moving to measurable implementation. Consumer and advertising trends remain resilient with AI agents seen as complementary demand-generation channels.

bullets.title: Hedge fund flows positive 8th consecutive month per GlobeOp; ETF equity flows at -2 sigma bearish, most negative since 1Q26
bullets.body: SS&C GlobeOp Index rose 65bp in September, the 8th consecutive month of positive hedge fund inflows, with +5.5% long-term flows and GlobeOp representing ~25% of SS&C revenue. Separately, JPM notes ETF flows show equities/credit at -2 sigma bearish level — the most negative since late 1Q26 — with CTAs stretched long crude (85th percentile) and short US bonds (5th percentile), a potentially contrarian setup.
